steps.name: Indra
steps.text: How'd things go on your end, Dagda?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Mr. Lane's still alive, but he's got a busted leg. His sworn brother didn't make it, though. I tried asking some old friends...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: None of them know when that brother passed away exactly. Might've been when trying to escape Norport, might've been some Sarkaz at the end of their tether during the allied counterattack...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Did you manage to see Mr. Lane himself?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I did. He works at the port now. He didn't bring up the old days, and he avoided talking about his crew.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But he thinks that now, he's living a good life.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Bloody hell.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I strolled around one of the factories we used to look after. It's full of little punks now. None of those youngsters have even heard of us Glasgow Gang.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: That pack of brats deserves a right trashing!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Did you swing by the old restaurant we always went to?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Torn down. Parliament sent some men over to get in touch with all the old shopkeeps. Anything so run-down it couldn't be fixed up, and whose owner was missing, was slated to be torn down and rebuilt.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: The pub on Sunset Street, Paul's Bar, the magazine stall that runt from Kazimierz ran... They're all gone.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Hannah...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I checked out that public cemetery they were talking about too. I couldn't find McClaren, or—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: (Choking back tears) Dammit, why don't these graves have names on them?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Stuff me, can't believe you caught me crying.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Let's head home already. Don't wanna leave Morgan waiting.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I thought... I thought the gym was going to be a rougher sight.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Looks to me like you've been taking care of the place this whole time.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I thought if you were still alive, you'd be coming back sooner or later. Doesn't matter how you look at it, I'm still part of the Glasgow Gang.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You didn't get on Duke Windermere's ship with us back then—

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I wasn't so far gone that I needed saving by the dukes.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: But... I gotta admit, I was being a right fool back then. After all that, I took some of the crew out to fight some devils hanging around Norport.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I ended up hearing about the Exemplars from them.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: You pulled off some crazy stunts I could never dream of. An army, hah... When the battle outside was in total chaos, some of the gang helped out on the front line with me.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: But there wasn't much we could do. All I got in the end were a few cuts and bruises—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You're Infected too?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Yep. Heard the same happened to Indra after she took a bad scrape on the battlefield not too long ago.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: She's real lucky she had friends like you there with her.
Morgan stares blankly ahead. She'd never considered that problem. Not even Indra herself had.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: No, no, that ain't right. Why do I feel all funny hearing you say that? Though I gotta admit I'm not sure what's not right about what you said.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Hah, whatever you say. Anyway, if you ever get the chance, tell Siege I said sorry.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: If you stick around you can tell her yourself.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: My Glasgow Gang's long gone. Since you're coming back, it's only right that I head out.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Did Delphine not come back with you?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She's standing by Vina's side.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Hah, sounds like you lot had a squabble too. I heard about her mum from a broadcast... Doesn't matter who she might be, at least she's got some nerve.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Where you headed off to next?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Norport needs more hands to rebuild it, and the port's busy shuttling in goods from outside all day every day. Me and my crew are gonna keep an eye on it.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: And then... And then I'll head into Central to bash in some merchant bastard's head—Err...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: That's only a maybe. Norport's changed, Morgan.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: The folks I know are gone, and the shops too. There's some new gang of brats that's popped up. Don't know their arse from their elbow yet they're still trying to fight for dominance...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Anyway, I'm giving the gym back to you lot.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Parliament talked a big game in that broadcast of theirs. I talked it over with some of the boys. We'll wait a spell, then head over to some other dukedom to see what's what.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: We'll find a new turf.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: A new turf, a new beginning. I'll need some time to forget a few things.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Morgan, was that Cador leaving just now?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Yep.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: He came to say goodbye, and decided to hand this back to us while he was at it.
She pulls out a butterfly knife from her pocket. It's badly scratched, but the emblem of the Glasgow Gang can still be clearly seen.
Baird's butterfly knife. Hannah would recognize it anywhere. It was her who insisted on engraving that emblem once she beat Baird, after all.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Cador found it on the body of a cleaner... He couldn't find Baird herself, though.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I went there too.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: All I found was some stuff on the wall I didn't get. It's almost all gone, what with all the rain. But I'm sure...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I'm sure she was there. I saw her handwriting.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: 'I hope so too'...

a.text: 'I hope so too.'
What did Baird hope for? We thought about it long and hard, but we were never able to make sense of it.

spans.text: What did Baird hope for? We thought about it long and hard, but we were never able to make sense of it.

a.text: Her wishes had already been washed back into Norport's soil by the rain.

spans.text: Her wishes had already been washed back into Norport's soil by the rain.

a.text: We decided not to dwell on it much longer.

spans.text: We decided not to dwell on it much longer.

a.text: We never could guess her last little secret.

spans.text: We never could guess her last little secret.

a.text: She's definitely having a good laugh at us right now.

spans.text: She's definitely having a good laugh at us right now.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I remember that whenever we went to the video shop, Baird hated weepy scenes about grieving the most.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Yeah. She never thought death was worth being all that sad for.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Pass the knife to me. I'll think of a way to hang it up on the wall.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Then I'll go get some drinks. To celebrate us coming home, and a toast to Baird!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Should we wait for Vina?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She ain't got the time to come.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: But just in case—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Then we'll hold off right before we get completely pissed, Hannah.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Booze waits for no man.

a.text: That day, without having to say a word on the matter, we all drank our drinks real slow.

spans.text: That day, without having to say a word on the matter, we all drank our drinks real slow.

a.text: We were waiting for one more person.

spans.text: We were waiting for one more person.

a.text: It seems there was a lot of chit-chat going on that day. Not that we remember any of it after the hangover.

spans.text: It seems there was a lot of chit-chat going on that day. Not that we remember any of it after the hangover.

a.text: All I remember is that Hannah and I got in a fight, and Dagda's brow got itself another scar. Why? None of us knew.

spans.text: All I remember is that Hannah and I got in a fight, and Dagda's brow got itself another scar. Why? None of us knew.

a.text: If Vina were there, it'll all be fine. She always stayed the most sober out of all of us, and she'd remember for us.

spans.text: If Vina were there, it'll all be fine. She always stayed the most sober out of all of us, and she'd remember for us.

a.text: But she never showed up that day.

spans.text: But she never showed up that day.

steps.name: Nervous Mercenary
steps.text: I dragged the body back, Boss.

steps.name: Nervous Mercenary
steps.text: But... Will this really be okay? I mean, snatching away the corpse of a condemned criminal from right under Parliament's nose—

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Did you really think you could take that away without some silent approval from above?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: What of the Columbian?

steps.name: Nervous Mercenary
steps.text: He's not in the best of moods... Boss, do we really need him to carry these goods? What if—

spans.text: He's not in the best of moods... Boss, do we really need
to carry these goods? What if—

steps.text: Millscar says nothing. The mercenary sighs.

steps.name: Nervous Mercenary
steps.text: Alright, I get it. Look, Boss, I'm not trying to make you mad. But ever since Parliament made a move on us, everyone's been on edge.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: It doesn't concern you lot.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: I'll handle the Columbian.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Eliseo. I presume I don't need to introduce myself.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Millscar. I've heard about you.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Good, no need to waste words then. I need you to see this batch of goods out of Londinium safely.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: You will, of course, receive payment. I can send this 'corpse' along with you.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Leave the city, and go as far away from it as you can.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Her name is Diane, Millscar.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Who she is isn't important to me.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: What's important is that she doesn't show her face again in Londinium.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: You call this payment? Making someone who just got home leave again?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Eliseo, you are well aware she cannot stay in the city. As far as everyone is concerned, she is dead. Hanged from the gallows.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Vina made a mistake. So long as this person is alive and within the city, sooner or later someone is going to use her as a knife to stab Vina in the back.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: *sigh* She really must learn to be more decisive.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: You know the condition of her infection better than I do, Eliseo. She doesn't have long.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: You're welcome to refuse, of course. But I will still help Vina settle this matter. In my own way.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I know your story, Millscar. Or rather, Lady Allerdale Cumberland.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: There's a lot of versions of it out there, but they all agree you really did fit with the title of 'Cumberland the Ever on High', once upon a time.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Fine, I'll get Diane out of here. I can take better care of her back in Columbia.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Happy?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: You're a good man, Eliseo. She's lucky to have made a friend in you.

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Get ready. You could be leaving at any time.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: You either die a hero, or you live long enough to see yourself become the villain.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Did you ever think you'd turn out this way?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Why ask just me?

steps.name: Millscar
steps.text: Countless heroes lived through the war. From the most radiant of them to those that none remember. I too am curious as to how they will change in the face of reality.
Lying down amidst the meadow, the soldier senses a slight itch. The cold wind blows at the stalks of grass, and their tips tickle her face.
Is this what the land of the dead is like? She opens her eyes and sees someone most unexpected.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Huh—Wha—?!

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: You're awake.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: It's me, Eliseo. You shouldn't just go off on your own to do dangerous stuff without a word, Diane.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I-I remember standing atop the gallows...

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: You're dead, at least to those who witnessed the execution.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Before we left, I asked the people at Rhodes Island to give you the once-over. It's not looking too good.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: A lot of your major organs have already begun to crystallize. In other words, Originium is replacing those organs.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: So... I'm not dead? Am I lucky or unlucky?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I'm not sure if the Speaker knew about this beforehand...

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: So it was Vina who let me go? That's rather foolish of her.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: To tell you the truth, I really don't get some of you people. *sigh* Sorry, Diane. I'm afraid you can't go back to Londinium.
Only now does she realize they are no longer in Londinium. She sees the tell-tale giant tracks laid down by the nomadic city not too far off in the distance.
Just ahead of them, Sarkaz children run around in the meadow, waving at her as they pass.
Most displaced Sarkaz have lost the light in their eyes to confusion. They can go anywhere, but nowhere can they call home.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I'll be taking you to Columbia, Diane. I might be able to do more for you there.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Alright then. Columbia, eh...?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I still remember saying that if I get the chance, I'd love to see the place you keep talking about.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: How far are we from Columbia, Eliseo?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Well, still very far away. Let me get out my map—

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Will I be able to make it there in my condition? Walking the whole way?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: ...I see. Could you promise me one thing, Eliseo?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I know what you're going to ask, Diane.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: When the day comes, I'll bring you home. I'll bring you back to Londinium.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I'm rather curious myself as to how much the city would have changed by the time we return.

a.text: The day we went back to the gym and got drunk, I had a dream.

spans.text: The day we went back to the gym and got drunk, I had a dream.

a.text: In that dream, there was a tomb, all dressed up to the nines. Our names were carved onto the plaques inside it—

spans.text: In that dream, there was a tomb, all dressed up to the nines. Our names were carved onto the plaques inside it—

a.text: 'Morgan', Kate Morrigan... 'Indra', Hannah Jackson
'Dagda', Isabelle Montague... 'Baird', Brigit Lucan
Outside the tomb, there was a blazing carriage, and atop it sat a golden lion. He was calling my name.

spans.text: Outside the tomb, there was a blazing carriage, and atop it sat a golden lion. He was calling my name.

a.text: Vina Victoria.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Mmfh... Vina...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: ...A blanket? Who put this blanket on me?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Urgh, my head hurts real bad. What time is it—
Morgan, didn't I tell you not to drink like a sodding wino all the time?
Hah, considering how wild Hannah and the rest can get, shouldn't you be looking after them?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Eh...? Vina? Vina!
Morgan nimbly launches herself out of the sofa, leaping over the short table to throw herself at Vina.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina, you came over!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I thought... I thought...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You thought what?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Why didn't you wake me, Hannah?!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Weren't you yapping and yowling yesterday about how she definitely wasn't coming?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Look at you. You turned out the most excited out of all of us.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: No I'm not!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Stubborn prick.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Quiet down, Morgan. Dagda's still asleep.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: (Mmph...)
The one resting her head atop Indra's lap twitches her ears, still lost within a lovely drunken dream.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Seems like Dagda drank the most out of you lot. I tidied up a lot of empty bottles.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: She must've been in a real rotten mood, Vina.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Sorry.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I just hope I'm not too late.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Well of course you're not!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Wasn't what you said yesterday, Morgan.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: (Shut it, Hannah!)

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Welcome home, Vina!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I was really hoping to pop in earlier, but there's simply far too much to handle over at Parliament.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Then... How'd you...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'm afraid I've given Horn another headache to deal with.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I suspect she'll only just have discovered I slipped away—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Then does that mean you need to head back?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I can't run away from my responsibilities.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But I owe you all an apology.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina, you don't need to—

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Eh? Siege? Vina!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: How long've I been asleep?!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Relax, Vina's only just arrived back.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That knife hanging on the wall—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: It's hers. Cador brought it back.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Cador?!

a.text: Vina never brought up having to head back the whole day, but we all knew—

spans.text: Vina never brought up having to head back the whole day, but we all knew—

a.text: That the Siege Vina, the boss of the Glasgow Gang, the ever-victorious king of the 'Slobberknocker', and (one of) my best friend(s) could leave us at any moment.

spans.text: That the Siege Vina, the boss of the Glasgow Gang, the ever-victorious king of the 'Slobberknocker', and (one of) my best friend(s) could leave us at any moment.

a.text: So I was loathe to lose a single moment where I could tell Vina about all the changes in Norport that she hadn't had the chance to see yet...

spans.text: So I was loathe to lose a single moment where I could tell Vina about all the changes in Norport that she hadn't had the chance to see yet...

a.text: Cador, Mr. Lane, the video shop...

spans.text: Cador, Mr. Lane, the video shop...

a.text: The reworked port, the rebuilt stores, a handful of old friends who rushed home after hearing the news...

spans.text: The reworked port, the rebuilt stores, a handful of old friends who rushed home after hearing the news...

a.text: Of course, who could forget the inexperienced little buggers who wanted to 'take over our gym'. After Vina beat them all to kingdom come with a smile on her face, they apologized by way of a few cartons of beer, and said they wanted to join us—

spans.text: Of course, who could forget the inexperienced little buggers who wanted to 'take over our gym'. After Vina beat them all to kingdom come with a smile on her face, they apologized by way of a few cartons of beer, and said they wanted to join us—

a.text: Seems like Norport's forgotten about us, but I don't think that's such a bad thing.

spans.text: Seems like Norport's forgotten about us, but I don't think that's such a bad thing.

a.text: The war really was over.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Do you still remember this place?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Why don't we get back to our little games, see who's fastest this time around?
Before Vina has even finished speaking, Indra has already begun to set off.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Hannah, you lousy cheat!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: She didn't say nothing about a countdown. I'm still the champ here!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: You've gotten slower ever since your injury, Hannah.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Say that after you've caught up.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Eh? Wha—?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: What's going on? Wait for me!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Don't fall behind, Delphine! Follow me!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Hear that, Del? You're a real slowpoke!
Several figures speed through the streets, and a few workers heading home after work give an inquisitive glance at the brash crew.
They can't quite seem to remember who this gang is—
'Must be another bunch of outsiders just arrived at Norport. Maybe.'
High above the gaps between the factories, the Glasgow Gang return to a favorite spot of theirs.
Here, they can look down upon the squatting factories, and look out at the Shard's pointed peak over at Central.
It was here that they started, and it was here that they left home. After a long period of wandering about, they have finally returned to this familiar place.
But—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I left a glass for Baird.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Sure you don't want a tipple, Dagda?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: No thank you. I'm not going to embarrass myself in front of Vina again.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I'll give your share to her, then.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Just fruit juice for you, Del?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Don't call me that. I'm still not too used to alcohol.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Suit yourself. I'll keep watch over you all.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Hell yeah! Finally, the part where we can start bloody drinking!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: To Baird! To the Glasgow Gang!

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: To Baird! To the Glasgow Gang!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: To Rhodes Island! To the Exemplars!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: To everyone who fought in the war!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: And, and, to all those who risked their lives coming home!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: To all those who live, and who left... To all those still by our side...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: To all those who shed blood and tears, to all those who struggle in darkness and in pain...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: ...To Victoria.

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: To Victoria!
There is no need for sorrow. The living engrave the moment in their memories, while those who left leave behind their hopes and dreams.
The fowlbeasts croon as they spiral overhead, echoing their words.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: You heading off too, Delphine?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Only for a short while. I need to go back to Lynncardine. Shearer will come along to recuperate.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: If you ever get real fed up of those lousy bastards, you can always come back here.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: This is your home too.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Of course I will! I promised Vina, after all.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: If there's ever a day you feel like it's all too much for you, Vina—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'll come back.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But I think I can handle it.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I hope the Londiniers can live in peace and happiness, and I hope that everyone can live their best lives. It's what they deserve.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Everyone should be like us. Smiling, without a tear in sight or an empty belly to be heard.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I'm not going to let everything we've accomplished go to waste.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: If someone tries to take it from us, I'll be fighting back.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Just like how we looked after this place back then.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Vina, Alexandrina, either's fine. There's no difference the way I see it. No?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: *burp*—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: If Baird were here, that's what she'd want me to do.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: You're right, Vina.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I really do hope so...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: To the Glasgow Gang. To all of you.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Welcome home, everyone.

a.text: Vina left us on the morning of the day after. She didn't let us see her off. Maybe she didn't want to wake us.

spans.text: Vina left us on the morning of the day after. She didn't let us see her off. Maybe she didn't want to wake us.

a.text: In truth, we were all awake. I watched her change into those clothes I was never fond of, and walk off on her lonesome towards Central Londinium.

spans.text: In truth, we were all awake. I watched her change into those clothes I was never fond of, and walk off on her lonesome towards Central Londinium.

a.text: I hope Vina managed to get a real good night's sleep, the best she's had in a long while. After all, it's only when she's at home that she doesn't need to think about anything.

spans.text: I hope Vina managed to get a real good night's sleep, the best she's had in a long while. After all, it's only when she's at home that she doesn't need to think about anything.

a.text: I spent the entire night writing down everything that happened the day Vina came home, no matter how big or small.

spans.text: I spent the entire night writing down everything that happened the day Vina came home, no matter how big or small.

a.text: I believe there will come a day that you, Vina, will read these words I wrote down.

spans.text: I believe there will come a day that you, Vina, will read these words I wrote down.

a.text: They might not be of too much use, but they can help you remember some of the more easily-forgotten things.

spans.text: They might not be of too much use, but they can help you remember some of the more easily-forgotten things.

a.text: Vina, do you still remember that dream I wrote about earlier?

spans.text: Vina, do you still remember that dream I wrote about earlier?

a.text: In that dream, there was a tomb, all dressed up to the nines. Our names were carved onto the plaques inside it—

spans.text: In that dream, there was a tomb, all dressed up to the nines. Our names were carved onto the plaques inside it—

a.text: Outside the tomb, there was a blazing carriage, and atop it sat a golden lion. He was calling my name.

spans.text: Outside the tomb, there was a blazing carriage, and atop it sat a golden lion. He was calling my name.

a.text: Vina Victoria.
I dreamt I was you.
I dreamt of a time I was all old and withered, some afternoon decades after I lost touch with my Glasgow friends...

spans.text: I dreamt of a time I was all old and withered, some afternoon decades after I lost touch with my Glasgow friends...

a.text: I walked into the tomb that 'Siege' built for the gang.

spans.text: I walked into the tomb that 'Siege' built for the gang.

a.text: I cherish that unforgettable memory that is no longer mine. I cherish the tale that started in Norport.

spans.text: I cherish that unforgettable memory that is no longer mine. I cherish the tale that started in Norport.

a.text: Vina, from the day you put on those clothes, I knew...

spans.text: Vina, from the day you put on those clothes, I knew...

a.text: In the end, you walk alone. You have no choice but to walk alone.

spans.text: In the end, you walk alone. You have no choice but to walk alone.

a.text: I'm sorry. There's no way for us to help you, or to stay by your side...

spans.text: I'm sorry. There's no way for us to help you, or to stay by your side...

a.text: But I wanted to let you know, we will always be here.

spans.text: But I wanted to let you know, we will always be here.

a.text: The Glasgow Gang will always be here.

spans.text: The Glasgow Gang will always be here.

a.text: To you, Vina Victoria.
